newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Brussels bourse debates IBt Euro NM listings.
newsitem.headline: Brussels bourse debates IBt Euro NM listings.

text.p: The Brussels bourse authorities on Wednesday will discuss whether and when Belgian cancer treatment firm International Brachytherapy (IBt) can start trading on the EURO.NM, Brussels' new small capitalisation market, a bourse official told Reuters on Wednesday.
Earlier this month the bourse said it was questioning the firm about legal claims against it before it could give the go-ahead for a listing.

IBt said earlier this month that U.S. company Theragenics Corp had lodged a civil complaint with a court in Georgia against IBt and its founders, claiming the latter had appropriated business secrets and confidential information belonging to Theragenics. IBt's managers are former founders and employees of Nasdaq-listed competitor Theragenics.

The bourse official said the bourse would also discuss a possible second listing, which could come as early as April. The official indicated this could be British hosiery and clothing maker Pex Plc, a 38 percent unit of Belgian textile holding company Uniwear.
The official said there were two other potential candidates, Belgian Synergia and Ecopolis.
"A possible listing for Ecopolis would be for after the summer," the official said.

Synergia is a holding company specialised in buying companies in financial trouble and reselling them after a turnaround has been achieved. Former IBM-Belgium director Tony Mary is one of the directors of the group.

Ecopolis is a Brussels-based producer of "intelligent glass recycling boxes", which crush and sort glass bottles and send radio signals to a central collection site when the box is full. Its systems are being tested in a Brussels suburb. Proceeds of a listing would be used to fund expansion in all major Belgian cities.

The Brussels EURO.NM - or New Market - is part of a wider project to form a federation of similar markets in Paris, Amsterdam and Frankfurt, rivalling the recently set up pan-European Brussels-based Easdaq market.
The Paris Nouveau Marche has been running for several months, Frankfurt's New Market opened earlier this month.
